findings.evidence: <select id="dob-day-select" autocomplete="bday-day" required=""> <select id="dob-month-select" autocomplete="bday-month" required=""> <select id="dob-year-select" autocomplete="bday-year" required="">
findings.fix: Use three short text fields for day, month and year, with the numeric input mode.
findings.violation: A date the person knows by heart is picked from three drop-downs, the year from 60 options.

findings.evidence: <input id="street-input" name="street_address" type="text" autocomplete="address-line1" required=""> is required on a form whose heading is 'Create your account' and whose submit button reads 'Create account'.
findings.fix: Limit this form to what creating an account needs (for example name, email and password). Move address, phone, shipping-speed and date-of-birth fields to checkout or profile completion, where their purpose is evident, and drop or explain the company-website, membership-number and contact-time fields.

instances.evidence: Required phone field, justified only by 'We will text you about delivery updates.', a later-step (shipping) reason, not account creation.
Required postal-code field, part of a home address an account does not need.
Required choice of shipping speed, a decision that belongs to an order, not account creation.
Required company-website field with no stated use in creating a personal account.
Required membership-number field, an answer a new account would not yet have.
Required account-number field, a second identifier alongside the membership number, with no stated use.
Required free-text field of unstated purpose.
Three required selects for day, month and year of birth, with no stated use in creating an account.

findings.violation: The task this form performs, named by its heading 'Create your account' and its submit label 'Create account', is creating an account, but the form requires a home address, a phone number justified only by delivery, a shipping speed, a company website, two different account-type numbers, a vague contact-time field, and a date of birth before the account can be created; none of these answers is used to create an account, and the shipping-related ones could be asked when an order is placed instead.

findings.evidence: <input id="postal-input" name="postal_code" type="text" autocomplete="postal-code" required="" size="3"> (size=3)
findings.fix: Size the field to show at least 5 characters.
findings.violation: This postal code field shows 3 characters, too few to show a typical value whole while it is typed and checked.

findings.fix: Loosen the pattern to accept every valid way of writing the value, and normalise it after submission.
findings.violation: The pattern on this phone field rejects valid values such as +44 20 7946 0958; 020 7946 0958.

findings.evidence: <button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button> sits between the 'Preferred contact time' field (#contacttime-input) and the 'Date of birth' fieldset (#row-dob); the primary submit, <button id="submit-btn" type="submit">Create account</button>, carries no declared style at all.
findings.fix: Move 'View details' out of the field sequence (before the first field, or placed and styled clearly as secondary after the primary submit), and give the primary submit at least as much visual weight as any secondary action.
findings.violation: A secondary action sits above fields still to be filled (the date-of-birth day, month and year selects), and its declared padding and font size give it more emphasis than the unstyled primary submit, so a person reaching it may believe the form has ended or press the wrong action.

findings.evidence: <label for="name-input">Full name</label> (line 11) and <label for="legalname-input">Your name</label> (line 62) both collect the person's name in the same form.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate name field, or rename and justify one as capturing a genuinely distinct value (for example a legal name that may differ from a display name).
findings.violation: The form asks for the person's name twice, once as 'Full name' (#name-input) and again as 'Your name' (#legalname-input); creating an account does not need the answer a second time.

findings.evidence: font-size: 13px declared by its inline style
findings.fix: Set the field's font size to at least 16 pixels.
findings.violation: The text in this field is 13 pixels, below the 16 pixels at which a phone stops zooming the page on focus.
This web address field is type text, so a phone does not show the keyboard built for it.
